title: JOIN
body:
An operation that combines rows from two tables into one result set by matching on a condition, normally a [[Foreign Key]] pointing at a [[Primary Key]] — combining two shelves' information in a single trip instead of two.

The variants worth knowing: an **INNER JOIN** returns only rows with a match on both sides; a **LEFT JOIN** returns every row from the left table, filling in nulls where the right side has no match (the one you want for "all products, with their reviews if any"). The whole operation executes **on the database server** — the app server sends a query and receives the combined result, which is why one join is usually far cheaper than fetching two sets and stitching them together in application code. That mistake, made in a loop, is the N+1 query problem. Join performance depends heavily on a [[Database Index]] existing on the joined columns.
